IV. Chandragupta II used Deva titles.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Chandragupta II was known as Vikramaditya and was also called Devagupta, Devashri and Devaraja. These were among the Deva titles used by him.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

Statement A: Piyadassi was a name used in Ashoka’s inscriptions.
Statement B: Priyadarshi was a name used in Ashoka’s inscriptions.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Ashoka used both Piyadassi and Priyadarshi as names in his inscriptions.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Gautamiputra Satakarni held the royal title Rajaraja.
Reason (R): Rajaraja was a royal title associated with Gautamiputra Satakarni.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Gautamiputra Satakarni held the title Rajaraja, and Rajaraja is specifically identified as his associated royal title.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. Iltutmish held the title Sultan.
II. Iltutmish held the title Sultan-i-Azam.
III. Sultan-i-Azam was a sovereign title.
IV. Balban was known as Zil-i-Ilahi.
V. Zil-i-Ilahi means shadow of God.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: I, II, III, IV and V
mcqs.explanation: Iltutmish held the titles Sultan and Sultan-i-Azam, with Sultan-i-Azam identified as a sovereign title. Balban was known as Zil-i-Ilahi, meaning shadow of God.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
 a. Padshah
 b. Ghazi
 c. Babur’s title adopted at Kabul
 d. Babur’s title assumed after the victory at Khanwa

List-II
 i. Kabul, 1504
 ii. Victory at Khanwa, 1527
 iii. Padshah
 iv. Ghazi
mcqs.explanation: Babur adopted the title Padshah at Kabul in 1504 and assumed the title Ghazi after his victory at Khanwa in 1527. Thus, Babur’s Kabul title was Padshah and his Khanwa-associated title was Ghazi.

mcqs.question: What is the meaning of the title ‘Shah Jahan’?
mcqs.explanation: ‘Shah Jahan’ means ‘King of the World’.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Alamgir means ‘Conqueror of the World’.
Reason (R): Alamgir was the title of Aurangzeb.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true: Alamgir means ‘Conqueror of the World’ and was the title of Aurangzeb. However, Aurangzeb’s association with the title does not explain its meaning.

mcqs.question: Which title of Samudragupta reflected his Vaishnavite association?
mcqs.explanation: Samudragupta held the title ‘Param Bhagavata’, identified in the sheet as a Vaishnavite title.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Kanishka and other Kushana rulers used the title Devaputra.
Reason (R): Devaputra was an imperial title.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The title Devaputra was used by Kanishka and Kushana rulers, and it denoted an imperial title.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Harshavardhana was also known as Shiladitya.
Statement B: Shiladitya was a title associated with Pulakeshin II.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true: Shiladitya was an alternative title or name of Harshavardhana. Statement B is false because Pulakeshin II was associated with the title Satyashraya.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Satyashraya was a title of Pulakeshin II.
II. Satyashraya was a title associated with the Chalukyas.
III. Pulakeshin II was known by the title Gangaikonda Chola.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. Pulakeshin II held the Chalukya title Satyashraya. Gangaikonda Chola was the title of Rajendra I.

mcqs.question: Rajendra I acquired the title ‘Gangaikonda Chola’ after which achievement?
options: The conquest of the Saka rulers
mcqs.explanation: Rajendra I was known as Gangaikonda Chola after his northern or Ganga campaign.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. Qutbuddin Aybak
 b. Qutbuddin Aybak
 c. Balban
 d. Rajendra I

List-II
 i. Zil-i-Ilahi
 ii. Gangaikonda Chola
 iii. Sipahasalaar
 iv. Quran Khwan
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Aybak–Sipahasalaar, Aybak–Quran Khwan, Balban–Zil-i-Ilahi, and Rajendra I–Gangaikonda Chola.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements about Qutbuddin Aybak are correct?

I. He was known as Sipahasalaar.
II. He was known as Quran Khwan for his melodious Quran recitation.
III. He held the title Zil-i-Ilahi.
IV. He was known as Gangaikonda Chola.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. Zil-i-Ilahi was Balban’s title, while Gangaikonda Chola was Rajendra I’s title.

mcqs.question: What did the title ‘Zil-i-Ilahi’ mean in relation to Balban?
mcqs.explanation: Balban’s title Zil-i-Ilahi meant ‘Shadow of God’. His other title, Niyabat-i-Khudai, meant God’s representative.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Farid Khan acquired the title Sher Khan after killing a tiger.
Statement B: Sher Khan was the title bestowed on Bairam Khan by Akbar.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true: Farid Khan acquired the title Sher Khan after killing a tiger. Statement B is false because Akbar bestowed the title Khan-i-Khanan on Bairam Khan.

mcqs.question: Which of the following are alternative names associated with Shankaracharya?
mcqs.explanation: The sheet identifies Shankar and Shree Shankaracharya as alternative names associated with Shankaracharya.

mcqs.question: What was the meaning of Ashoka’s title ‘Devanampiya’ or ‘Devanampriya’?
mcqs.explanation: ‘Devanampiya’ or ‘Devanampriya’ was an epithet of Ashoka meaning ‘Beloved of the Gods’.

mcqs.question: Which of the following were the earliest extant coins, dating from the 7th–6th century BC to the Mauryan period?
mcqs.explanation: Punch-marked or Aahat coins are identified in the notes as the earliest extant coins. They were mainly silver and are dated from the 7th–6th century BC to the Mauryan period.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Chandragupta I was the first Gupta ruler to issue coins.
Chandragupta II's silver coins were associated with victory over the Sakas.
Chandragupta II was the first Gupta ruler to issue coins.
Gupta gold coins were called Dinara or Dinar.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement alters the ruler. Chandragupta I, not Chandragupta II, was the first Gupta ruler to issue coins.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Vima Kadphises was the first Kushana ruler to issue gold coins.
Reason (R): Vima Kadphises introduced the regular use of gold coins on a large scale.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The notes specifically state that Vima Kadphises was the first Kushana ruler to issue gold coins and introduced their regular large-scale use.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Agathocles
(b) Kanishka
(c) Yaudheyas
(d) Iltutmish

List-II
(i) Regular coinage with Delhi as capital
(ii) Buddha on coins
(iii) Bilingual legends in Greek and Brahmi
(iv) Standing Kartikeya with peacock
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Agathocles–bilingual Greek and Brahmi legends; Kanishka–Buddha on coins; Yaudheyas–standing Kartikeya with peacock; Iltutmish–regular coinage with Delhi as capital.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about Satavahana coinage:

I. It included lead, copper, bronze, silver and potin.
II. It included gold coins.
III. Potin was an alloy or mixture of copper, silver and lead.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and III are correct. The notes list lead, copper, bronze, silver and potin in Satavahana coinage, and describe potin as a copper, silver and lead alloy or mixture. The notes explicitly state that Satavahana coinage had no gold.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct about Gupta coinage?

I. Gupta gold coins were called Dinara or Dinar.
II. Gupta silver coins were called Rupaka.
III. The maximum number of Gupta coins was found at Bayana or Bharatpur in Rajasthan.
IV. Chandragupta II's silver coins were associated with victory over the Sakas.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct according to the notes: Gupta gold coins were Dinara/Dinar, silver coins were Rupaka, the major Gupta coin hoard was at Bayana or Bharatpur in Rajasthan, and Chandragupta II's silver coins were linked with victory over the Sakas.

mcqs.question: The coins of Strato II, an Indo-Greek ruler, were made of which metal?
mcqs.explanation: Strato II is associated with important Indo-Greek lead coins.

mcqs.question: The discovery at Bairat is associated with how many coins of Menander?
mcqs.explanation: The Bairat coin discovery consisted of 16 coins of Menander.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Indo-Greek rulers introduced the circulation of gold coins in north-western India.
Statement B: The notes associate the introduction of gold circulation in north-western India with the Indo-Greek rulers.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The notes state that Indo-Greek rulers introduced the circulation of gold coins in north-western India.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Yaudheyas
(b) Saka-Kshatrapas
(c) Chastana
(d) Iltutmish

List-II
(i) Gold-silver ratio of 1:35
(ii) Regular coinage with Delhi as capital
(iii) Standing Kartikeya with a peacock
(iv) Silver and copper coins, with copper relatively rare
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Yaudheyas–standing Kartikeya with a peacock, Saka-Kshatrapas–1:35 ratio, Chastana–silver and relatively rare copper, and Iltutmish–regular coinage with Delhi as capital.

mcqs.question: What was the gold-to-silver ratio associated with the Saka-Kshatrapas?
mcqs.explanation: The gold-to-silver ratio of the Saka-Kshatrapas was 1:35.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about Chastana is incorrect?
options: Chastana is associated with the Karddamaka line.
Chastana issued silver and copper coins.
Copper coins of Chastana were relatively rare.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that Chastana issued only gold coins. The notes mention his silver and copper coins, with copper relatively rare.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Potin was used in Satavahana coinage.
Reason (R): Potin was an alloy or mixture of copper, silver and lead.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the composition of potin explains its identification as an alloy or mixture used in Satavahana coinage.

mcqs.question: Who was the first Gupta ruler to issue coins?
mcqs.explanation: Chandragupta I was the first Gupta ruler to issue coins.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Chandragupta I was the first Gupta ruler to issue coins.
II. Chandragupta II's silver coins were associated with victory over the Sakas.
III. Chandragupta II was known as Sakari.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Chandragupta I was the first Gupta coin issuer, while Chandragupta II's silver coins were linked with victory over the Sakas and he was known as Sakari.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the major Gupta coin hoard?
options: A major Gupta coin hoard was found at Bayana.
The major Gupta coin hoard was found at Delhi.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the location Delhi. The major Gupta coin hoard was found at Bayana, Bharatpur, Rajasthan.

mcqs.question: The silver coin of Iltutmish mentioned in the notes weighed how much?
mcqs.explanation: The silver currency of Iltutmish is mentioned as weighing 175 grams.

mcqs.question: Which Muslim ruler's coins bore the image of Lakshmi?
mcqs.explanation: The notes identify Muhammad Ghori as the Muslim ruler whose coins bore Lakshmi.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Iltutmish's coins bore the Khalifa's name after his recognition by the Abbasid Caliph.
Reason (R): Recognition by the Abbasid Caliph preceded the appearance of the Khalifa's name on Iltutmish's coins.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the recognition by the Abbasid Caliph explains why the Khalifa's name appeared on Iltutmish's coins.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Kushana gold coins circulated on a wider, regular and large scale.
II. Kushana copper coins circulated extensively.
III. Lead was a major metal in Satavahana coinage.
IV. Gold was a major metal in Satavahana coinage.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct. Gold was not used in Satavahana coinage according to the notes, so statement IV is incorrect.

mcqs.question: The early Kushana copper coinage is associated with which ruler?
mcqs.explanation: Kujula Kadphises is associated with early Kushana copper coinage. His coins were made of copper.

mcqs.question: Punch-marked coins in early India were mainly made of which metal?
mcqs.explanation: Punch-marked or Aahat coins of early India were mainly made of silver.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Agathocles
(b) Chandragupta II
(c) Iltutmish
(d) Muhammad Ghori

List-II
(i) Silver and copper coins
(ii) Silver coins featuring Sankarshana and Vasudeva
(iii) Coins bearing the Arabic Kalma
(iv) Silver Rupaka coins
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Agathocles—silver coins featuring Sankarshana and Vasudeva; Chandragupta II—silver Rupaka coins; Iltutmish—silver and copper coins; and Muhammad Ghori—coins bearing the Arabic Kalma.

mcqs.question: Who wrote the grammatical work Ashtadhyayi?
mcqs.explanation: Panini authored Ashtadhyayi, a work on grammar.

mcqs.question: Which work is associated with Abul Fazl's account of Akbar's administration and empire?
mcqs.explanation: Ain-i-Akbari deals with Akbar's administration and empire. Akbarnama concerns Akbar's reign.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Herodotus is known as the Father of History.
Reason (R): His work Historica deals with Indo-Persian relations.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true: Herodotus is identified as the Father of History, and Historica concerns Indo-Persian relations. The subject of the work does not explain the title itself.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Tolkappiyam is the oldest extant Tamil grammar.
Reason (R): It deals with grammar and poetics.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Tolkappiyam is described as the oldest extant Tamil grammar, and it deals with grammar and poetics. The latter fact does not explain why it is the oldest extant work.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Vishakhadatta wrote Mudrarakshasa, a Sanskrit drama associated with Chandragupta and Kautilya.
Dandin wrote Dashakumaracharita, concerning the adventures of ten princes.
Bharavi wrote Kiratarjuniyam, concerning the combat between Nala and Damayanti.
Kalidasa wrote Abhijnanashakuntalam, a Sanskrit drama.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the subject of Kiratarjuniyam. The work concerns the combat between Arjuna and Shiva; Nala and Damayanti are associated with Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Minhaj-us-Siraj wrote Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, a history of early Muslim rule.
Statement B: Ziauddin Barani wrote Tarikh-i-Firuzshahi, a work on Sultanate history.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is linked with Minhaj-us-Siraj, while Tarikh-i-Firuzshahi is linked with Ziauddin Barani.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Nannaya translated the Mahabharata into Telugu.
II. Tikkana was part of the Kavi Traya.
III. Yerrapragada translated the Mahabharata into Tamil.
mcqs.explanation: Nannaya and Tikkana are associated with the Telugu translation of the Mahabharata and the Kavi Traya. Yerrapragada also belongs to the Kavi Traya and the Telugu translation tradition, not a Tamil translation.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Yaska
(b) Amar Singh
(c) Varahamihira
(d) Kalhana

List-II
(i) Rajatarangini
(ii) Nirukta
(iii) Amarakosh
(iv) Panchasiddhantika
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Yaska–Nirukta, Amar Singh–Amarakosh, Varahamihira–Panchasiddhantika and Kalhana–Rajatarangini.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Ashvaghosha
(b) Al-Biruni
(c) Firuz Shah Tughluq
(d) Rana Kumbha

List-II
(i) Futuhat-i-Firuz Shahi
(ii) Sangeet Raj
(iii) Kitab-ul-Hind
(iv) Buddhacharita
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Ashvaghosha–Buddhacharita, Al-Biruni–Kitab-ul-Hind, Firuz Shah Tughluq–Futuhat-i-Firuz Shahi and Rana Kumbha–Sangeet Raj.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Patanjali
(b) Yaska
(c) Katyayana
(d) Amar Singh

List-II
(i) Mahabhashya — grammar and commentary
(ii) Nirukta — etymology
(iii) Varttika — grammar
(iv) Amarakosh — Sanskrit lexicon
mcqs.explanation: Patanjali wrote Mahabhashya, which deals with grammar and commentary. Yaska wrote Nirukta on etymology, Katyayana wrote Varttika on grammar, and Amar Singh wrote Amarakosh, a Sanskrit lexicon.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. Vatsyayana wrote Kamasutra, a classical Sanskrit work.
II. Kalidasa wrote Meghaduta, a Sanskrit poem.
III. Kalidasa wrote Kumarasambhavam, a Sanskrit poem.
IV. Kalidasa wrote Malavikagnimitram, a Sanskrit drama.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. Kamasutra is associated with Vatsyayana, while Meghaduta, Kumarasambhavam and Malavikagnimitram are works of Kalidasa; the first two are Sanskrit poetry and the last is a Sanskrit drama.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

Statement A: Buddhacharita deals with the life of Buddha.
Statement B: Ashvaghosha wrote Saundarananda, which is Buddhist Sanskrit literature.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Buddhacharita deals with the life of Buddha, and Ashvaghosha wrote Saundarananda, classified as Buddhist Sanskrit literature.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Harshavardhana was the royal author of Ratnavali.
Reason (R): Harshavardhana wrote Ratnavali.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Harshavardhana wrote Ratnavali, and this work is associated with him as its royal author.

mcqs.question: Which of the following works was written by Harshavardhana?
mcqs.explanation: Priyadarshika was written by Harshavardhana. Nirukta, Shishupalavadha and Saundarananda are associated respectively with Yaska, Magha and Ashvaghosha.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Harshavardhana was the royal author of Priyadarshika.
II. Harshavardhana wrote Nagananda.
III. Harshavardhana was the royal author of Nagananda.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Harshavardhana was the royal author of Priyadarshika and Nagananda, and Nagananda was also written by him as a royal author.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Tolkappiyar
(b) Ilango Adigal
(c) Vishakhadatta
(d) Vatsyayana

List-II
(i) Kamasutra
(ii) Silappadikaram
(iii) Tolkappiyam
(iv) Mudrarakshasa

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
mcqs.explanation: Tolkappiyar wrote Tolkappiyam, Ilango Adigal wrote Silappadikaram, Vishakhadatta wrote Mudrarakshasa, and Vatsyayana wrote Kamasutra.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Silappadikaram deals with Kannagi and Kovalan.
Statement B: Silappadikaram is a Tamil work.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Silappadikaram is a Tamil work dealing with Kannagi and Kovalan.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Sayana's Vedic commentaries had Vijayanagara patronage.
Reason (R): Sayana was a famous commentator on Vedic texts.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but Sayana's fame as a commentator does not explain the fact that his Vedic commentaries had Vijayanagara patronage. Sayana wrote Vedic commentaries and was a famous commentator on Vedic texts.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Amir Khusrau wrote Tughluqnama, a Persian historical work.
II. Amir Khusrau wrote Qiran-us-Sadain, a Persian work.
III. Amir Khusrau wrote Miftah-ul-Futuh, a Persian work.
IV. Amir Khusrau wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh-i-Alai, a Persian work.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. Tughluqnama, Qiran-us-Sadain, Miftah-ul-Futuh and Khazain-ul-Futuh-i-Alai were written by Amir Khusrau; Tughluqnama is specifically described as a Persian historical work, while the others are Persian works.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. Ashika was written by Amir Khusrau and is a Persian work.
2. Nuh Sipihr was written by Amir Khusrau and is a Persian work.
3. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri deals with Bengal and Bakhtiyar Khalji.
4. Hasan Nizami wrote Taj-ul-Maasir, which deals with early Turkish-period history.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. Ashika and Nuh Sipihr are Persian works by Amir Khusrau; Tabaqat-i-Nasiri deals with Bengal and Bakhtiyar Khalji; and Hasan Nizami wrote Taj-ul-Maasir on early Turkish-period history.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Tarikh-i-Mubarakshahi
(b) Kitab-ul-Hind
(c) Futuhat-i-Firuz Shahi
(d) Sangeet Mimansa

List-II
(i) Music
(ii) Indian religion, society, geography, culture and politics
(iii) Royal account
(iv) Sultanate history
mcqs.explanation: Tarikh-i-Mubarakshahi deals with Sultanate history; Kitab-ul-Hind deals with Indian religion, society, geography, culture and politics; Futuhat-i-Firuz Shahi is a royal account; and Sangeet Mimansa deals with music.

mcqs.question: Who wrote Tarikh-i-Mubarakshahi?
mcqs.explanation: Tarikh-i-Mubarakshahi was written by Yahya-bin-Ahmad Sarhindi.

mcqs.question: Kitab-ul-Hind is also known as which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: Kitab-ul-Hind is also known as Tahqiq-i-Hind.

mcqs.question: Which of the following works deals with music?
mcqs.explanation: Sangeet Raj deals with music.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. Babur wrote Tuzuk-i-Baburi.
II. Tuzuk-i-Baburi is also known as Baburnama.
III. Tuzuk-i-Baburi is an autobiography.
IV. Tuzuk-i-Baburi is written in Turkish.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct: Babur wrote Tuzuk-i-Baburi, also called Baburnama; it is an autobiography written in Turkish.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Kalila-wa-Dimnah
(b) Anwar-i-Suhaili
(c) Ayar-i-Danish
(d) Persian translation of Yogavasistha

List-II
(i) Nizamuddin Panipati
(ii) Abul Fazl
(iii) Nashrullah Shirazi Munshi
(iv) Mulla Kashifi Husain Waiz
mcqs.explanation: Nashrullah Shirazi Munshi translated Kalila-wa-Dimnah into Persian; Mulla Kashifi Husain Waiz wrote Anwar-i-Suhaili; Abul Fazl wrote Ayar-i-Danish; and Nizamuddin Panipati wrote a Persian translation of Yogavasistha.

mcqs.question:

Bhrigu Kachchha was also known as Bharuch.
Bharuch was located in western India and belonged to the Gupta period.
Bharuch was associated with trade with western countries and was an important port for North Indian trade with western countries.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the location: Bharuch was located in western India, not eastern India. Its other stated associations were the Gupta period and trade with western countries, including North Indian trade.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Arikamedu was located in South India, belonged to the Gupta-era trade network, and was a major centre of international trade.
Statement B: Kaveripattanam was located in South India, belonged to the Gupta-era trade network, and was a major centre of international trade.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Arikamedu and Kaveripattanam were South Indian centres in the Gupta-era trade network and each was associated with, and a major centre of, international trade.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Muziris was a major centre of international trade during the Gupta-era trade network.
Reason (R): Muziris belonged to the Gupta-era trade network.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true. Muziris was a major centre of international trade during the Gupta-era trade network and belonged to that network, but the reason does not correctly explain the assertion.

mcqs.question: Pratishthana was located in which of the following regions?
mcqs.explanation: Pratishthana was located in the Deccan.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Pratishthana was located in the Deccan and belonged to the Gupta-era trade network.
Statement B: Pratishthana was associated with international trade and was a major centre of international trade.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Pratishthana was a Deccan centre in the Gupta-era trade network. It was associated with international trade and was a major centre of international trade.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements correctly describe Sopara?
1. Sopara was located in western India.
2. Sopara belonged to the Gupta-era trade network.
3. Sopara was associated with international trade.
4. Sopara was a major centre of international trade.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements correctly describe Sopara: its location was western India, and it belonged to the Gupta-era trade network, being associated with and a major centre of international trade.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about Barberikam is incorrect?
options: Barberikam belonged to the Gupta-era trade network.
Barberikam was located in eastern India.
Barberikam was associated with international trade.
Barberikam was located in western India.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement places Barberikam in eastern India. Barberikam was located in western India; it belonged to the Gupta-era trade network and was associated with international trade as a major centre.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about Surat:
I. Surat was located in Gujarat.
II. Surat was located on the western coast.
III. Surat was associated with Mughal and European trade.
IV. Surat later had English, Dutch and French European trade.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. Surat was a Gujarat port on the western coast, associated with Mughal and European trade, and later had English, Dutch and French European trade.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Masulipatnam was located on the Coromandel Coast and was associated with European trade.
Statement B: Agra was associated with European trade.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Masulipatnam was a European-trade centre on the Coromandel Coast. Agra was also associated with European trade.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. Ahmedabad was located in Gujarat.
2. Ahmedabad was associated with European trade.
3. The English East India Company established a factory at Ahmedabad in 1619.
4. Baroda was located in Gujarat.
5. Baroda was associated with European trade.
6. The English East India Company established a factory at Baroda in 1619.
7. Broach was located in Gujarat.
mcqs.explanation: All seven statements are correct. Ahmedabad and Baroda were Gujarat locations associated with European trade, and English East India Company factories were established at both in 1619; Broach was also located in Gujarat.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Broach
(b) Armagaon
(c) Hariharpur
(d) Balasore

List-II
(i) Coromandel Coast; European trade; English EIC factory established in 1628
(ii) Odisha; eastern coast; European trade; English EIC factory established in 1633
(iii) Gujarat; European trade; English EIC factory established in 1619
(iv) Eastern coast; European trade; English EIC factory established in 1633

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mcqs.explanation: Broach was in Gujarat and had an English EIC factory established in 1619. Armagaon was on the Coromandel Coast and had an English factory in 1628; Hariharpur and Balasore were eastern-coast centres with English factories established in 1633, while Balasore was in Odisha.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Bhatkal was located in Karnataka and belonged to the Vijayanagara period.
Reason (R): Bhatkal was associated with Portuguese trade.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true: Bhatkal was located in Karnataka, belonged to the Vijayanagara period and was associated with Portuguese trade. The trade association does not explain its location or period.

mcqs.question: Who permitted Afonso de Albuquerque to construct a fort?
mcqs.explanation: Krishnadeva Raya permitted Afonso de Albuquerque to construct a fort.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Lothal was associated with West Asian trade and was an Indus Valley Civilization port connecting Asia with West Asia.
Statement B: Bharuch connected North India with western countries.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Lothal was an Indus Valley Civilization port linked with West Asian trade, while Bharuch connected North India with western countries.

mcqs.question: Who fought the Portuguese in the Battle of Swally?
options: The English East India Company at Agra
mcqs.explanation: Thomas Best fought the Portuguese in the Battle of Swally.

mcqs.question: What was the original name of Rani Lakshmibai?
mcqs.explanation: The notes identify Manikarnika as the original name of Rani Lakshmibai, who was born in Varanasi.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Chenab was known by the Vedic name Asakini.
Ravi was known by the Vedic name Parushni.
Jhelum was known by the Vedic name Vitasta.
Beas was known by the Vedic name Vitasta.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is the second one. The notes give Vipasa as the Vedic name of Beas; Vitasta was the Vedic name of Jhelum.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Pataliputra was a later capital of Magadha.
Reason (R): The capital of Magadha was shifted from Rajgriha to Pataliputra by Udayin.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The notes state that Rajgriha was the early capital of Magadha and that Pataliputra became the later capital after the shift by Udayin.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Aryavarta referred to Northern India, the land occupied by the Aryans.
Statement B: Madhya Desh was the region between the Himalayas and the Vindhyas.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true according to the notes. Aryavarta denotes Northern India or the land occupied by the Aryans, while Madhya Desh lies between the Himalayas and the Vindhyas.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Kabul River
(b) Kurram River
(c) Swat River
(d) Gandak

List-II
(i) Suvastu
(ii) Sadaneera
(iii) Kubha
(iv) Krumu
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Kabul River–Kubha, Kurram River–Krumu, Swat River–Suvastu and Gandak–Sadaneera.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Jaunpur was known as Shiraz-i-Hind during the Sharqi period.
II. Rupnagar was earlier known as Ropar.
III. Pundravardhana Bhukti was an ancient territorial designation for the North Bengal region.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are supported by the notes: Jaunpur had the sobriquet Shiraz-i-Hind during the Sharqi period, Rupnagar was earlier called Ropar, and Pundravardhana Bhukti was the ancient territorial designation of North Bengal.

mcqs.question: Kannauj was known by which ancient name?
mcqs.explanation: Kannauj is associated with the ancient name Mahodaya Shri.

mcqs.question: Mahodaya Shri is associated with which historical personality?
mcqs.explanation: Mahodaya Shri is associated with Mihir Bhoj.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Bundelkhand
(b) Aligarh
(c) Mahoba
(d) Muhammad-bin-Tughluq

List-II
(i) Jauna Khan
(ii) Koil
(iii) Jejakabhukti
(iv) Mahotsav Nagar
mcqs.explanation: Bundelkhand was known as Jejakabhukti, Aligarh as Koil, Mahoba as Mahotsav Nagar, and Muhammad-bin-Tughluq as Jauna Khan.

mcqs.question: What was the original or personal name of Muhammad-bin-Tughluq?
mcqs.explanation: Muhammad-bin-Tughluq's original or personal name was Jauna Khan.

mcqs.question: Genghis Khan was originally known by which name?
mcqs.explanation: Temujin or Temuchin was the original name of Genghis Khan.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Chenab
(b) Beas
(c) Ravi
(d) Jhelum

List-II
(i) Vitasta
(ii) Vipasa
(iii) Asakini
(iv) Parushni
mcqs.explanation: The Vedic/Rigvedic names were Chenab–Asakini, Beas–Vipasa, Ravi–Parushni, and Jhelum–Vitasta.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Saraswati was described by more than one title in the Rigvedic context.
Reason (R): Saraswati was called Matetama, Devitama and Naditama.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The three titles explain why Saraswati was described by more than one title: Matetama, Devitama and Naditama.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Saraswati was called Matetama, meaning “Best of all mothers.”
Statement B: Saraswati was called Devitama, meaning “Best of all rivers.”
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Matetama means “Best of all mothers,” whereas Devitama means “Best of all goddesses,” not “Best of all rivers.”

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Chitrotpala is the name of Mahanadi found in the Mahabharata.
II. Nilotapala is the name of Mahanadi found in the Vayu Purana.
III. Chitrotpala is the name of Mahanadi found in the Matsya Purana.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct: Mahanadi is called Chitrotpala in the Mahabharata and Matsya Purana, and Nilotapala in the Vayu Purana.

mcqs.question: Which name of the Indus is associated with its importance?
mcqs.explanation: Hiranyayi is the name associated with the importance of the Indus.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Brahmarshi Desh was an ancient geographical terminology.
Reason (R): Brahmarshi Desh referred to the land of seven rivers.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Brahmarshi Desh was an ancient geographical terminology, but the land of seven rivers was called Sapta-Sindhu.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are ancient geographical terms or territorial designations?
1. Brahmarshi Desh
2. Sapta-Sindhu
3. Pundravardhana Bhukti
4. Koil
mcqs.explanation: Brahmarshi Desh, Sapta-Sindhu and Pundravardhana Bhukti are ancient geographical or territorial designations. Koil was an early-medieval name of Aligarh.

mcqs.question: Rani Lakshmibai was born in which place?
mcqs.explanation: Rani Lakshmibai was born in Varanasi.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. The Gomal River was known as Gomati in the Vedic or Rigvedic period.
2. The Ghaggar River was known as Drishdvati in the Vedic or Rigvedic period.
3. Naditama means “Best of all rivers.”
4. Naditama means “Best of all goddesses.”
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Gomati was the Vedic/Rigvedic name of the Gomal River, Drishdvati was the name of the Ghaggar River, and Naditama means “Best of all rivers.” Statement 4 is incorrect; “Best of all goddesses” is the meaning of Devitama.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Kaushambi was the capital of Vatsa.
Statement B: Kaushambi was not the capital of Magadha.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. Kaushambi was the capital of Vatsa and was not the capital of Magadha.

mcqs.question: Which earlier/current-name transformation is associated with the Ahilyanagar district in Maharashtra?
mcqs.explanation: Ahmednagar was the earlier name associated with the Ahilyanagar district in Maharashtra, and the name underwent the transformation from Ahmednagar to Ahilyanagar.

mcqs.question: Nagar Mahoday Shri is best classified as which of the following in relation to Kannauj?
mcqs.explanation: Nagar Mahoday Shri was a sobriquet or title associated with Kannauj. It was not its ancient or original name.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Nagar Mahoday Shri was a sobriquet or title of Kannauj.
Reason (R): Nagar Mahoday Shri was not an ancient or original name of Kannauj.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true: Nagar Mahoday Shri was a sobriquet or title of Kannauj, and it was not its ancient or original name. However, the second statement does not explain the first.

17.title: Battles and Wars in Indian History

mcqs.question:
Arrange the following battles in chronological order:
A. Battle of Tarain (First)
B. Battle of Tarain (Second)
C. Battle of Plassey
D. Battle of Buxar
mcqs.explanation: The First Battle of Tarain was fought in 1191, the Second in 1192, Plassey in 1757 and Buxar in 1764.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) First Battle of Tarain
(b) Second Battle of Tarain
(c) Battle of Chausa
(d) Battle of Kannauj/Bilgram

List-II
(i) Sher Shah defeated Humayun
(ii) Prithviraj Chauhan's victory
(iii) Muhammad Ghori's victory
(iv) Sher Shah defeated Humayun
mcqs.explanation: The First Battle of Tarain was a Chauhan victory; the Second was won by Muhammad Ghori. Sher Shah defeated Humayun at both Chausa and Kannauj/Bilgram.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Kalinga War was a turning point in Ashoka's life.
Reason (R): The war strengthened Ashoka's association with Buddhism and Dhamma.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: The notes describe the Kalinga War as a turning point in Ashoka's life and state that it strengthened his association with Buddhism and Dhamma.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The First Carnatic War was fought from 1746 to 1748.
The Second Carnatic War was fought from 1750 to 1755.
The Battle of Wandiwash was fought in 1760.
The Third Carnatic War was fought from 1758 to 1763.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the period of the Second Carnatic War. The notes give it as 1749–54, not 1750–55.

mcqs.question: Who was associated with the Rashtrakuta-led confederacy in the Battle of Takkolam?
mcqs.explanation: The Battle of Takkolam involved Rajaditya and Krishna III, with Western Gangas and Vaidumbas; it was a major Chola–Rashtrakuta conflict.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat.
II. Babur defeated Rana Sanga in the Battle of Khanwa.
III. Babur won the Battle of Chanderi against Medini Rai.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: The notes state that Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat, Rana Sanga at Khanwa and Medini Rai at Chanderi.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Battle of Plassey established British control over Bengal.
Reason (R): The Battle of Plassey was associated with treachery.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are given in the notes. However, the note records treachery as an association of Plassey and separately identifies the establishment of British control over Bengal; it does not state that the former explains the latter.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Battle of Talikota weakened Vijayanagara.
Statement B: The Battle of Haldighati resulted in a Mughal victory.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The notes describe Talikota as a watershed battle that weakened Vijayanagara and record a Mughal victory at Haldighati.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following centre–leader pairs of the Revolt of 1857 are correctly matched?
1. Delhi — Bahadur Shah Zafar
2. Kanpur — Nana Sahib
3. Lucknow — Begum Hazrat Mahal
4. Jhansi — Rani Lakshmibai
mcqs.explanation: All four pairs are given in the notes as major centres and associated leaders of the Revolt of 1857.

mcqs.question: Who was the British commander in the Battle of Buxar?
mcqs.explanation: The Battle of Buxar in 1764 was a British victory under Major Hector Munro.

mcqs.question: On which date was the Battle of Pollilur fought?
mcqs.explanation: The notes date the Battle of Pollilur to 10 September 1780. It involved Haidar Ali and Tipu against Colonel Baillie.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The First Anglo-Maratha War ended with the Treaty of Salbai.
II. The Second Anglo-Maratha War was associated with Lord Wellesley and Peshwa Baji Rao II.
III. The Third Anglo-Maratha War established British supremacy over the Marathas.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: The notes associate the First Anglo-Maratha War with the Treaty of Salbai, the Second with Lord Wellesley and Peshwa Baji Rao II, and the Third with British supremacy over the Marathas.

mcqs.question: The Battle of 10 Kings is also known as which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: The Battle of 10 Kings is also called the Battle of Dasharajnya.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Sudas commanded his forces in the Battle of 10 Kings.
Reason (R): Sudas achieved a decisive victory in the Battle of 10 Kings.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true: Sudas commanded his forces and achieved a decisive victory. The victory does not explain the fact that he commanded the forces.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Sudas fought against a confederacy of 10 Kings in the Battle of 10 Kings.
Statement B: The Battle of 10 Kings is mentioned in the Rigveda.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. The battle was fought by Sudas against a confederacy of 10 Kings and is mentioned in the Rigveda.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Hydaspes:
I. It belongs to the ancient period.
II. It was part of Alexander's Indian campaign.
III. Alexander fought against Porus in this battle.
IV. Alexander and Porus were the leaders in this battle.
V. Alexander defeated Porus.
VI. The battle represents an Alexander–India linkage.
options: II, III, IV and VI only
I, IV, V and VI only
I, II, III and V only
I, II, III, IV, V and VI
mcqs.explanation: All six statements are correct. The Battle of Hydaspes was an ancient-period battle in Alexander's Indian campaign, fought between Alexander and Porus, ending in Alexander's victory and representing an Alexander–India linkage.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Period of the Kalinga War
(b) Power that fought against Kalinga
(c) Commander of the Mauryan forces
(d) Transformation associated with the Kalinga War

List-II
(i) Ancient period
(ii) Mauryas
(iii) Ashoka
(iv) Ashoka's transformation
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-i, b-ii, c-iii and d-iv. The Kalinga War was ancient, involved the Mauryas against Kalinga, was commanded by Ashoka, and led to Ashoka's transformation.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Takkolam:
I. It belongs to the early medieval period.
II. Rajaditya led the Chola side.
III. The Western Gangas were associated with the Rashtrakuta side.
IV. The Vaidumbas were associated with the Rashtrakuta side.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. Takkolam was an early medieval battle in which Rajaditya led the Chola side, while the Western Gangas and Vaidumbas were associated with the Rashtrakuta side.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: In the Battle of Takkolam, the Cholas fought against a Rashtrakuta-led confederacy, and the battle was a major Chola–Rashtrakuta conflict.
Statement B: The Battle of Takkolam resulted in a Rashtrakuta victory, and Rajaditya and Krishna III were associated with the battle.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Takkolam was a major Chola–Rashtrakuta conflict involving a Rashtrakuta-led confederacy, ended in Rashtrakuta victory, and was associated with Rajaditya and Krishna III.

mcqs.question: Who fought against Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain?
mcqs.explanation: Prithviraj Chauhan fought against Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain.

mcqs.question: Who led his side in the First Battle of Tarain?
mcqs.explanation: Prithviraj Chauhan led his side in the First Battle of Tarain.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Prithviraj Chauhan fought against Muhammad Ghori in the Second Battle of Tarain.
Reason (R): Muhammad Ghori led his side in the Second Battle of Tarain.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Prithviraj Chauhan and Muhammad Ghori were opposing leaders, but Muhammad Ghori's leadership does not explain the fact that Prithviraj fought against him.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) First Battle of Panipat
(b) Opponent faced by Babur
(c) Military equipment used in the battle
(d) Persons associated with the artillery

List-II
(i) Ibrahim Lodi
(ii) 1526
(iii) Artillery
(iv) Ustad Ali Quli and Mustafa
mcqs.explanation: The First Battle of Panipat took place in 1526; Babur fought Ibrahim Lodi, commanded his forces, and artillery was used. Ustad Ali Quli and Mustafa were associated with that artillery.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. The Battle of Khanwa took place in 1527; Babur fought against Rana Sanga and commanded his forces.
II. The Battle of Chanderi took place in 1528; Babur fought against Rai Medini and commanded his forces.
III. The Battle of Ghaghra took place in 1529; Babur fought against Afghan rulers, commanded his forces and achieved victory.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Khanwa, Chanderi and Ghaghra occurred in 1527, 1528 and 1529 respectively, with Babur as commander in each; Babur achieved victory in Ghaghra.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Battle of Chausa took place in 1539.
Statement B: Humayun fought against Sher Shah Suri in the Battle of Chausa, and Humayun and Sher Shah were its leaders.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Battle of Chausa took place in 1539, and its leaders were Humayun and Sher Shah, who fought against each other.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Humayun and Sher Shah were the leaders in the Battle of Kannauj or Bilgram.
Statement B: The Battle of Chausa preceded the Battle of Bilgram.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Humayun and Sher Shah were the leaders in the Battle of Kannauj or Bilgram. The Battle of Chausa occurred before the Battle of Bilgram.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Second Battle of Panipat:
I. It took place in 1556.
II. Akbar's forces fought against Hemu's forces.
III. Akbar's side won the battle.
IV. The battle consolidated Mughal power.
mcqs.explanation: The Second Battle of Panipat took place in 1556 between Akbar's forces and Hemu's forces. Akbar's side won, and the victory consolidated Mughal power.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Battle of Talikota
(b) Combined Deccan Sultanates
(c) Opponent of the combined Deccan Sultanates
(d) Significance of the Battle of Talikota

List-II
i. 1565
ii. Vijayanagara
iii. Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Golconda
iv. Vijayanagara was defeated; the battle was a watershed battle
mcqs.explanation: The Battle of Talikota took place in 1565. The combined Deccan Sultanates consisted of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Golconda, fought Vijayanagara, and defeated it in this watershed battle.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the Battle of Haldighati?
options: Man Singh led the Mughal side in the battle.
The Battle of Haldighati took place in 1576.
The Battle of Haldighati is associated with Akbar and Sher Shah.
Mughal forces fought against Rana Pratap's forces.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement alters the associated figure: the Battle of Haldighati is associated with Akbar and Rana Pratap, not Sher Shah. The other statements correctly identify its year, opponents and Mughal commander.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) First Carnatic War
(b) Result concerning Madras
(c) Treaty associated with the First Carnatic War
(d) Year of the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle

List-II
i. British regained Madras
ii. English fought against the French
iii. Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle
iv. 1748
mcqs.explanation: The English fought the French in the First Carnatic War, during which the British regained Madras. The associated Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle was concluded in 1748.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Ambur:
I. It took place in 1749.
II. Muzaffar Jang and Chanda Sahib fought against Anwar-ud-din.
III. The French supported Muzaffar Jang and Chanda Sahib.
IV. Anwar-ud-din was defeated in the battle.
mcqs.explanation: The Battle of Ambur took place in 1749. Muzaffar Jang and Chanda Sahib, supported by the French, fought Anwar-ud-din, who was defeated.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Battle of Ambur
(b) Chanda Sahib
(c) Battle of Ambur

List-II
(i) Anwar-ud-din was killed
(ii) Gained control of the Carnatic
(iii) Part of the Second Carnatic War
mcqs.explanation: Anwar-ud-din was killed in the Battle of Ambur; Chanda Sahib gained control of the Carnatic; and the battle was part of the Second Carnatic War.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Second Carnatic War was inconclusive.
Reason (R): English- and French-backed Indian factions fought in the Second Carnatic War.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The notes state that the war was inconclusive and that English- and French-backed Indian factions fought in it, but they do not state that the latter was the reason for the inconclusive result.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Plassey:

I. The British fought against Siraj-ud-daula.
II. Robert Clive led the British side.
III. The battle marked the beginning of British supremacy.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct: the British fought Siraj-ud-daula, Robert Clive led the British side, and the battle marked the beginning of British supremacy.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Third Carnatic War
(b) Count Lally
(c) British victory in the Third Carnatic War
(d) Treaty of Paris

List-II
(i) British fought against the French
(ii) Led the French side
(iii) French power in India ended
(iv) Concluded in 1763 and associated with the Third Carnatic War
mcqs.explanation: The Third Carnatic War was fought between the British and French; Count Lally led the French side; British victory ended French power in India; and the Treaty of Paris, associated with the war, was concluded in 1763.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Wandiwash:

I. The British fought against the French.
II. British forces fought against Count Lally's French forces.
III. The British achieved victory.
IV. The battle was decisive in the Third Carnatic War.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. The Battle of Wandiwash involved British forces and Count Lally's French forces, ended in British victory, and was decisive in the Third Carnatic War.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Buxar:

I. The British fought against Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II.
II. The British achieved victory.
III. The battle led to greater consolidation of British supremacy.
IV. The Treaty of Allahabad was concluded in 1765.
V. The Treaty of Allahabad was associated with the Battle of Buxar.
options: I, II, III, IV and V
I, III, IV and V only
mcqs.explanation: All five statements are correct. The Battle of Buxar was fought against Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II; the British won, consolidated their supremacy further, and were associated with the Treaty of Allahabad concluded in 1765.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The First Anglo-Mysore War took place from 1767 to 1769.
Statement B: The British fought against Mysore in the First Anglo-Mysore War.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The First Anglo-Mysore War took place from 1767 to 1769 and involved the British fighting against Mysore.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the First Anglo-Mysore War:
I. Haidar Ali led Mysore in the war.
II. Haidar Ali was victorious in the war.
III. The Treaty of Madras was concluded in 1769.
IV. The Treaty of Madras was associated with the First Anglo-Mysore War.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. Haidar Ali led Mysore to victory in the First Anglo-Mysore War, and the associated Treaty of Madras was concluded in 1769.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Pollilur:
Statement A: Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan fought against Colonel Baillie.
Statement B: Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan defeated Colonel Baillie.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan fought Colonel Baillie and defeated him in the Battle of Pollilur.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Second Anglo-Mysore War:
I. It took place from 1780 to 1784.
II. The British fought against Mysore.
III. Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan were associated with the war.
IV. It was a major Anglo-Mysore conflict.
V. Haidar Ali allied with the Nizam during the war.
VI. Haidar Ali allied with the Marathas during the war.
options: I, II, III and IV only
I, II, III, IV, V and VI
II, III, IV, V and VI only
I, II, IV, V and VI only
mcqs.explanation: All six statements are correct. The Second Anglo-Mysore War lasted from 1780 to 1784, involved the British and Mysore, and was associated with Haidar Ali, Tipu Sultan and Haidar Ali's alliances with the Nizam and the Marathas.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Porto Novo:
I. It took place in July 1781.
II. Haidar Ali fought against Sir Eyre Coote.
III. Sir Eyre Coote led the British side.
IV. The British achieved victory.
V. It was part of the Second Anglo-Mysore War.
options: I, II, III, IV and V
I, III, IV and V only
mcqs.explanation: All five statements are correct. The Battle of Porto Novo occurred in July 1781, where Sir Eyre Coote led the victorious British against Haidar Ali as part of the Second Anglo-Mysore War.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the First Anglo-Maratha War:
Statement A: It involved the British and the Marathas.
Statement B: The British suffered defeat in the war.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The First Anglo-Maratha War involved the British and the Marathas, and the British suffered defeat.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Second Anglo-Maratha War:
Statement A: It involved the British and the Marathas.
Statement B: It was associated with the Subsidiary Alliance.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Second Anglo-Maratha War involved the British and the Marathas and was associated with the Subsidiary Alliance.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Third Anglo-Maratha War involved the British and the Marathas.
Reason (R): Lord Hastings was associated with the Third Anglo-Maratha War.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but Lord Hastings's association with the war does not explain why the war involved the British and the Marathas.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Kharda:
Statement A: The Battle of Kharda is also called the Battle of Khurda.
Statement B: The Battle of Kharda took place in 1795.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Battle of Kharda is also known as the Battle of Khurda, and it took place in 1795.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Marathas fought against the Nizam in the Battle of Kharda.
Statement B: The Nizam was defeated in the Battle of Kharda.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The Battle of Kharda was fought between the Marathas and the Nizam, and the Nizam was defeated.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Battle of Chillianwala took place on 13 January 1849.

options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the opponents in the battle do not explain why it took place on 13 January 1849.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) British side in the Battle of Chillianwala

(d) Annexation of Punjab

mcqs.explanation: Lord Gough led the British side, Sher Singh led the Sikh side, the battle was undecided, and Punjab was annexed by the British in 1849.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Revolt of 1857 involved rebels and the British.
II. The Kanpur episode took place in 1857, and rebels fought against the British there.
III. The Lucknow episode took place in 1857, and rebels fought against the British there.
IV. The Jhansi episode took place in 1857, and rebels fought against the British there.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct: the revolt involved rebels and the British, and Kanpur, Lucknow and Jhansi were episodes in 1857 involving fighting between rebels and the British.

mcqs.question:

(i) Kunwar Singh

(iv) 1857
mcqs.explanation: The Bihar episode took place in 1857; rebels fought against the British, Kunwar Singh was the associated leader, and Bihar was a major centre of the revolt.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Kannauj:

mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. The Battle of Kannauj was also known as the Battle of Bilgram, took place in 1540, and was fought between Humayun and Sher Shah.

mcqs.question: Who commanded his forces in the First Battle of Panipat?
mcqs.explanation: Babur commanded his forces in the First Battle of Panipat.

mcqs.question: The First Carnatic War was fought between which of the following powers?
mcqs.explanation: The First Carnatic War was fought between the English and the French.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Third Carnatic War is incorrect?
options: Count Lally was associated with the French side.
The British defeated the French in the Third Carnatic War.
The French defeated the British in the Third Carnatic War.
The Third Carnatic War took place from 1758 to 1763.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement reverses the result of the war: the British defeated the French in the Third Carnatic War.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Pollilur:
I. Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan led the Mysore side.
II. Colonel Baillie led the opposing side.
III. The battle involved the Mysore side under Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan against the opposing side under Colonel Baillie.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan led the Mysore side, while Colonel Baillie led the opposing side in the Battle of Pollilur.

mcqs.question: The Third Anglo-Maratha War ended in which year?
mcqs.explanation: The Third Anglo-Maratha War ended in 1818.

18.title: Coronations and Accessions of Indian Rulers

mcqs.question: Krishnadeva Raya was enthroned in which year and reigned during which period?
mcqs.explanation: Krishnadeva Raya was enthroned in 1509 and reigned from 1509 to 1529.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding Aurangzeb is incorrect?
options: His second coronation followed victories at Khajwa and Deorai.
His second coronation took place on June 5, 1659.
He was first coronated on July 21, 1658, at Delhi.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the place: Aurangzeb's first coronation was recorded on July 21, 1658, but the notes do not specify Delhi for it. Delhi is associated with the second coronation entry.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Shivaji assumed the title Chhatrapati in 1674.
Reason (R): Gaga Bhatta, also known as Vishweshwar, performed Shivaji's formal coronation.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Shivaji's formal coronation in 1674, performed by Gaga Bhatta, was associated with his assumption of the title Chhatrapati.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Iltutmish
(b) Akbar
(c) Shivaji-II
(d) Ashoka

List-II
(i) Placed on the throne in 1689
(ii) Post-coronation visit to Lumbini in the 20th year
(iii) Declared himself Sultan at Delhi in 1211
(iv) Accession at Kalanaur on February 14, 1556
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Iltutmish–declared himself Sultan at Delhi in 1211; Akbar–accession at Kalanaur on February 14, 1556; Shivaji-II–placed on the throne in 1689; Ashoka–post-coronation visit to Lumbini in the 20th year.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Rajaraja-I's accession to the throne took place in 985 and marked the beginning of the golden era of the Chola Empire.
Statement B: After Rajaram's death, Tarabai placed her four-year-old son on the throne as Shivaji-II.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true according to the notes. Rajaraja-I acceded in 985, while Tarabai placed her four-year-old son on the throne after Rajaram's death.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Iltutmish
(b) Akbar
(c) Shivaji
(d) Ashoka

(ii) Worshipped Buddha’s birthplace at Lumbini
(iii) Succession was supported or approved by Turkish nobles
(iv) Was coronated at Raigarh
mcqs.explanation: Iltutmish’s succession after Qutbuddin Aibak was supported or approved by Turkish nobles. Akbar was under 14 at coronation, Shivaji was coronated at Raigarh, and Ashoka worshipped Buddha’s birthplace at Lumbini.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Bairam Khan was associated with Akbar’s accession or coronation.

Statement A is false, Statement B is true

mcqs.question: Lumbini is also known by which of the following names?
mcqs.explanation: Lumbini is also called Rummindei.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements about Lumbini are correct?

I. Lumbini was exempted from the Bali tax.
II. Ashoka reduced Lumbini’s land revenue to one-eighth.
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. Lumbini was exempted from the Bali tax, and Ashoka reduced its land revenue to one-eighth.

mcqs.question: In which year did Iltutmish become associated with the declaration of himself as Sultan?
mcqs.explanation: Iltutmish declared himself Sultan in 1211.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Iltutmish declared himself Sultan at Delhi.
Aurangzeb’s first coronation took place at Kalanaur.
Akbar was enthroned at Kalanaur, Gurdaspur, Punjab.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the place of Aurangzeb’s first coronation. It took place at Delhi, not Kalanaur.

mcqs.question: Which title did Iltutmish declare himself?
mcqs.explanation: The exam fact associated with Iltutmish is that he declared himself Sultan.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Turkish nobles supported and approved Iltutmish’s succession.
Reason (R): Iltutmish’s succession followed the death of Qutbuddin Aibak.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The notes connect the Turkish nobles’ support for Iltutmish’s succession with the succession following Qutbuddin Aibak.

mcqs.question: On which date was Akbar enthroned?
mcqs.explanation: Akbar was enthroned on February 14, 1556.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Akbar was enthroned at Kalanaur.
Statement B: Kalanaur was identified with Gurdaspur, Punjab, in the enthronement record.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false

mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Akbar’s enthronement took place at Kalanaur, Gurdaspur, Punjab.

mcqs.question: How many times was Aurangzeb coronated?
mcqs.explanation: Aurangzeb was coronated twice.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I

(b) Aurangzeb’s second coronation

(ii) July 21, 1658

mcqs.question: On which date did Aurangzeb undergo his second coronation?
mcqs.explanation: Aurangzeb’s second coronation took place on June 5, 1659.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Aurangzeb’s second coronation followed victories at Khajwa and Deorai.

options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

mcqs.question:

mcqs.question: Who defeated Muhammad Ghori in the Gujarat conflict of 1178?
mcqs.explanation: Muhammad Ghori suffered his first defeat in India in the Gujarat conflict of 1178 against Mularaja-II / Bhimdev-II, with Naika Devi acting as regent.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Anwar-ud-din was killed in the Battle of Ambur in 1749.
The Battle of Pollilur in 1780 was a major British defeat.
Humayun defeated Sher Shah Suri in the Battle of Chausa in 1540.
The Battle of Wandiwash was fought in 1760, and Count de Lally was defeated.

mcqs.question:

options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Deccan Sultanates opposing Vijayanagara included Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Golconda, which explains the conflict described as the Battle of Talikota.

mcqs.question:

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

III. The Battle of Devara / Daurah was fought on the banks of the Gomati.

mcqs.question:

mcqs.explanation: The correct sequence is Panipat (1526), Khanwa (1527), Chanderi (1528) and Ghaghra (1529): B, D, C, A.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan in the 2nd Battle of Tarain.
Reason (R): The 2nd Battle of Tarain, fought in 1192, reversed the result of the 1st Battle of Tarain fought in 1191.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan in the 2nd Battle of Tarain in 1192. This reversed the result of the 1st Battle of Tarain of 1191, and the reason describes the significance of the second battle.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

mcqs.question:

options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true

Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Rao Jaitsi, the ruler of Bikaner, defeated Kamran Mirza in the Bikaner conflict.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Battle of Kanauj, also called the Battle of Bilgram, took place in 1540.

options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Battle of Devara, also called Daurah, took place in 1532.
Reason (R): Humayun defeated Afghan rebels in the Battle of Devara.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the Battle of Sirhind?
options: Humayun lost effective control over North India in 1540
mcqs.explanation: The Battle of Sirhind took place in 1555, in which Humayun defeated Afghan forces.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the 1st Battle of Panipat.
II. The 1st Battle of Panipat marked the beginning of Mughal rule in North India.
III. Babur defeated Rana Sanga in the Battle of Khanwa.
IV. Babur assumed the title of Ghazi after the Battle of Khanwa.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat, defeated Rana Sanga at Khanwa, assumed the title of Ghazi after Khanwa, and the 1st Battle of Panipat marked the beginning of Mughal rule in North India.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true

mcqs.explanation: Babur defeated Medini Rai at Chanderi and defeated Afghan rulers or forces in the Battle of Ghaghra.

mcqs.question: What was the key result of the Battle of Ghaghra?
options: It marked the beginning of Mughal rule in North India

mcqs.question:
